title: ServePath Latency Splineboard: p50/p95/p99 with IO-mode Cohort Comparator
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
Build a ServePath-focused latency dashboard ("Splineboard") that compares p50/p95/p99 across model and route cohorts with a strict split
between streaming and non-streaming IO modes. The goal is an operational view that helps SREs and
runtime engineers quickly triage regressions caused by kernel selection, KV-cache miss patterns, or
prefix-batch behavior.

Why this work matters:
- Multiple recent incidents showed tail latency spikes correlated with a higher proportion of
  streaming requests on certain model-route combos; existing boards surface totals but not IO-mode
  splits with cohorting.
- This board will be the canonical surface for on-call runbooks and for product/infra to measure the
  impact of batching/quantization/engine upgrades.

Scope / panels planned:
1) Cohort selector: model family, route name, customer tier, and time-range. Presets: top-10 heavy
   routes last 24h / 7d.
2) P50/P95/P99 spline lines over time with stacked overlay showing streaming vs non-streaming percent
   of traffic. Tooltips show sample counts and median request size.
3) ServePath decomposition waterfall (avg) for selected cohort: network + proxy + runtime init +
   token-gen. Compare streaming vs non-streaming side-by-side.
4) KV-cache miss rate & prefix-hit ratio timeseries per cohort.
5) Error rate heatmap (5xx/4xx) split by IO-mode and model variant.
6) Trace-links table: top N example traces for p99 regressions with link to tracing UI and PRAGMA
   annotations (kernel selection, quantization flag).

Acceptance criteria:
- Dashboard populates for any model-route combination within 60s of query time range change.
- p50/p95/p99 calculations use the same aggregated aggregation functions as the SLO service to avoid
  discrepancies.
- Streaming vs non-streaming split is computed from the request metadata field io_mode with fallback
  heuristic based on presence of streaming websocket_id.
- Traces linked contain an auto-annotated tag (servepath.cohort) so engineers can pivot from dashboard to
  spans.

Implementation notes / decisions made so far:
- Telemetry pipeline: we will use the metrics-kafka topic for per-request latency histograms and a
  materialized timeseries in Clickhouse. This avoids high-cardinality joins at query time.
- For pxx calculations we will store HDR histograms at 1s rollup for 24h and 1m rollup for 7d.
- Tracing hooks: added servepath.cohort labels at the ingress layer (ENG-276482 setup) to ensure traces
  and request metrics can be correlated.
- To reduce alert fatigue, p99 drift alerts will be gated behind a minimum sample threshold (N>=100).

Outstanding risks / open questions:
- Cardinality explosion for combining model-variant, route, and customer-tier. Plan: only show top-K
  cohorts by QPS with on-demand filters for arbitrary cohorts.
- Accuracy of streaming detection for older clients that embed streaming via chunked HTTP. We will run
  a 7-day audit query and add heuristics if necessary.

Work completed so far:
- Prototype queries in Clickhouse: saved as metrics.query.SERVE_SPLINE_v1 (link below).
- Instrumented io_mode tagging at ingress (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/1248).
- Initial dashboard skeleton created in Grafana (https://grafana.internal.redwood/serve-spline/510238).

- Clickhouse prototype queries: https://git.redwood/observability/queries/-/blob/main/serve_spline.sql
- Ingress PR (io_mode tags): https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress/pull/1248

Next steps / plan for remainder of cycle:
- (Week 1) Finalize query perf improvements: add precomputed per-cohort HDR rollups; iterate on
  sample-threshold gating.
- (Week 2) User testing with SRE on-call and runtime engineers; collect feedback and add two
  additional panels for KV-cache latency breakdown.
- (Week 3) Bake into runbooks and wire p99 drift alerts into PagerDuty with manual escalation rules.

Review notes / feedback to address:
- PM (Jordan Ellis): prefer adding a compact mobile-friendly view for on-call.
- Design (Maya Park): simplify cohort selector and add clearer affordances for streaming vs non-streaming
  legends.

Testing / rollout checklist:
- Unit tests for query generation and histogram rollup code.
- Load test dashboard queries against staging rollout with synthetic traffic (scripts in /observability/load/).
- Incremental rollout: enable for internal tenants first, then beta customers, then all.
